html:
Tertullian was a Christian writer from Carthage, active around 200 CE, and the first major author of Christian theology in Latin. He is often called the father of Latin Christianity.

Trained in rhetoric and perhaps law, he became a Christian as an adult and wrote fiercely in defence of the faith against pagans and heretics. He was the first to use the Latin word trinitas, Trinity, for God. His line that the blood of the martyrs is seed of the Church became a proverb.

In later life he joined a strict movement called Montanism. Through him and later Augustine, Roman Africa shaped the theology of the Western church. See also Roman Africa and Christianity.
sum: Tertullian was a Christian writer from Carthage, active around 200 CE, and the first major author of Christian theology in Latin. He is often called the father of Latin Christianity.
